name: Compound light microscope
summary: Magnifies small specimens such as cells and microorganisms using a set of lenses and a built-in light source.
uses: Viewing prepared slides of cells and tissues
Examining microorganisms in biology and microbiology labs
tips: Start with the lowest-power objective, then move up
Carry it with one hand under the base and one on the arm
Clean lenses only with lens paper

name: UV-Vis spectrophotometer
summary: Measures how much light a sample absorbs at a chosen wavelength, which can be used to work out its concentration.
uses: Finding the concentration of coloured solutions
Following how fast a reaction proceeds
tips: Zero the instrument with a blank sample first
Handle cuvettes by their frosted sides
Wipe off drips before inserting a cuvette

name: Benchtop centrifuge
summary: Spins samples at high speed so that heavier components separate from lighter ones.
uses: Collecting cells or precipitates as a pellet
tips: Always balance tubes opposite each other
Keep the lid closed until the rotor has stopped
Never exceed the rated speed of the tubes

name: Analytical balance
summary: Weighs small masses very precisely inside a glass draft shield that blocks air currents.
uses: Checking the mass of a product
tips: Tare the balance with the empty container on the pan
Close the draft-shield doors before reading
Keep it level and away from vibration

name: pH meter
summary: Measures how acidic or alkaline a solution is using a glass electrode.
tips: Calibrate with standard buffer solutions before use
Rinse the electrode between samples
Store the electrode moist, never dry

name: Micropipette
summary: A hand-held pipette that measures and dispenses very small, adjustable volumes of liquid using disposable tips.
uses: Loading samples into plates and gels
tips: Use a fresh tip for every sample
Press the plunger slowly and smoothly
Never lay it down with liquid in the tip

name: Magnetic hotplate stirrer
summary: Heats and stirs liquids at the same time by spinning a magnetic stir bar inside the vessel.
tips: The top plate can stay hot after it is switched off
Never heat flammable solvents on an open hotplate
Add the stir bar before switching the stirrer on

name: Bunsen burner
summary: A gas burner that produces a single open flame for heating, sterilising and combustion.
tips: Tie back long hair and keep the area clear
Light it with the air hole closed, then open it for a blue flame
Never leave a lit burner unattended

name: Fume hood
summary: A ventilated enclosure that draws fumes away from the user while working with volatile or hazardous chemicals.
uses: Handling volatile solvents and concentrated acids
Protecting the user from breathing in fumes
tips: Work at least 15 cm inside the sash
Keep the sash as low as practical
Don't use the hood for storing chemicals

name: Beaker
summary: A cylindrical container with a pouring spout, used for mixing, heating and holding liquids.
tips: Its graduations are approximate, so measure volumes with a cylinder or pipette
Use borosilicate glass when heating
Check for chips and cracks before use

name: Conical (Erlenmeyer) flask
summary: A flask with a flat base, conical body and narrow neck, which reduces splashing when the contents are swirled.
tips: Swirl gently from the wrist rather than shaking
The narrow neck can be stoppered or covered with foil
Use a clamp when heating

name: Round-bottom flask
summary: A spherical flask that heats evenly, used with heating mantles and distillation apparatus.
tips: It cannot stand on its own, so support it on a cork ring or clamp
Never fill it more than about half full when heating
Inspect for star cracks before applying vacuum

name: Volumetric flask
summary: A flask calibrated to hold one exact volume at a set temperature, shown by a line on its neck.
tips: Fill until the bottom of the meniscus sits on the line
Read the line at eye level
Don't heat it, as heat changes the calibrated volume

name: Graduated cylinder
summary: A tall, narrow cylinder with markings for measuring liquid volumes more accurately than a beaker.
tips: Read the bottom of the meniscus at eye level
Choose the smallest cylinder that holds your volume
Stand it on a flat surface before reading

name: Test tubes and rack
summary: Small glass tubes for holding, mixing and heating small amounts of chemicals, kept upright in a rack.
tips: Point the open end away from people when heating
Fill no more than about a third when heating
Use a test-tube holder for hot tubes

name: Filter funnel
summary: A cone-shaped funnel used with filter paper to separate solids from liquids, or to pour into narrow necks.
tips: Fold the filter paper into a cone that fits snugly
Keep the liquid level below the top of the paper
Rest the stem against the inside of the receiving flask

name: Petri dishes
summary: Shallow lidded dishes used to grow microorganisms on agar and to hold small samples.
tips: Label the base, not the lid
Incubate dishes upside down to stop condensation dripping
Seal and dispose of cultures safely

name: Burette on retort stand
summary: A long graduated tube with a tap at the bottom, used to add precise volumes of liquid during titrations.
tips: Rinse with the solution you are about to use
Remove the air bubble below the tap before starting
Read the meniscus at eye level

name: Fire extinguisher
summary: A portable device for putting out small fires. Laboratories usually keep types that are suitable for electrical and chemical fires, such as CO₂ or dry powder.
uses: Putting out small fires before they spread
tips: Remember PASS: Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep
Only tackle small fires, with an exit behind you
Check the pressure gauge and service tag

name: Eyewash station
summary: Delivers a gentle stream of water to flush chemicals or particles out of the eyes.
uses: First response to chemical splashes in the eyes
tips: Flush for at least 15 minutes, holding the eyelids open
Keep the path to it clear at all times
Test it regularly so the water stays clean

name: First aid kit
summary: A stocked kit for treating minor injuries such as cuts and burns until further help arrives.
tips: Know where it is before you start work
Report every injury, however small
Restock it after use

name: Safety goggles
summary: Close-fitting eye protection that shields against chemical splashes, dust and flying fragments.
uses: Eye protection during any chemical work
Protection when handling glassware under pressure or heat
tips: Wear them whenever chemicals are in use, not just when you are pouring
Choose goggles rated for chemical splashes
Clean and store them away from dust

name: Lab coat
summary: A long-sleeved protective coat that keeps chemical splashes and spills off your skin and clothes.
tips: Keep it buttoned with the sleeves down
Take it off before leaving the lab
Remove it straight away if it is contaminated

name: Nitrile gloves
summary: Disposable gloves that protect the hands from many chemicals and biological samples.
tips: Check the chemical's safety data sheet for the right glove type
Change gloves straight away if they tear or are splashed
Never touch door handles or phones with gloved hands
